Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft, and the most openly speculative page in this directory - which is why its confidence is low rather than medium. 3.2.0 halves Counterattack and Counter Swarm damage from 150% to 75% and, in the same breath, gives Spiritborn a new paragon board called Swarm of Storms granting roughly 80% increased damage to storm skills. Read together, those look like a compensation: take the new board and get the damage back. There is one problem, and this page exists because of it rather than in spite of it - no source consulted says which Spiritborn skills carry the Storm tag. The official notes name the board and its effect and stop. The class's own knowledge file lists thirteen Season 14 skills and tags none of them. So this build cannot be written; only the experiment that would decide whether it can be written. Everything below is a shell for running that experiment, and if the answer to test 1 is 'none', the correct outcome is to delete this page rather than to defend it.

Rotation
  1. Rushing Claw through the pack and let the swarms do the work - the base build's loop, unchanged, because this page is a control rather than a build.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] The base build's rotation, unchanged, because this stage is a control rather than a build. Rushing Claw through the pack, swarms do the work.
Move on when [ptr] Test 1 answered: you have read the skill tags and know whether any usable Spiritborn skill is a Storm skill. Do not progress this page on an assumption.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged control rotation.
Move on when [ptr] The multiplier measured, or the page retired.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged.
Move on when [ptr] A verdict written down: either a storm-tagged skill exists and this build should be rewritten around it, or none does and this page should be retired.

Pushing — [ptr] There is nothing honest to write here. This page has one job, which is to get the Storm-tag question answered on the PTR and reported back; a push stage exists only because the schema requires four stages, and the correct thing to do at this point is to play spiritborn-hybrid-counterswarm-direct instead.

Uniques
  • ring 1 [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts, which is how you should gear this experiment - it is not worth a farm. Live route: Lord Zir, The Darkened Way east of Kyovashad, Fractured Peaks; 1x Lair Key from the Blood Maiden in Helltide. Where →

How to run them

[ptr] 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries; this is the Season 14 Spiritborn pairing carried over and labelled as carried over, tree picks included: Subo's four are the same four whichever Spiritborn hires him, so inheriting them borrows no build decision. Nothing else about this page is more finished than it looks.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft, and the most openly speculative page in this directory - which is why its confidence is low rather than medium. 3.2.0 halves Counterattack and Counter Swarm damage from 150% to 75% and, in the same breath, gives Spiritborn a new paragon board called Swarm of Storms granting roughly 80% increased damage to storm skills. Read together, those look like a compensation: take the new board and get the damage back. There is one problem, and this page exists because of it rather than in spite of it - no source consulted says which Spiritborn skills carry the Storm tag. The official notes name the board and its effect and stop. The class's own knowledge file lists thirteen Season 14 skills and tags none of them. So this build cannot be written; only the experiment that would decide whether it can be written. Everything below is a shell for running that experiment, and if the answer to test 1 is 'none', the correct outcome is to delete this page rather than to defend it.

Rotation
  1. Rushing Claw through the pack and let the swarms do the work - the base build's loop, unchanged, because this page is a control rather than a build.

This page has one job, which is to get the Storm-tag question answered on the PTR and reported back; a push stage exists only because the schema requires four stages, and the correct thing to do at this point is to play spiritborn-hybrid-counterswarm-direct instead.

Reasoning

Hypothesis[ptr] 3.2.0's Swarm of Storms board is the intended compensation for the Counterattack and Counter Swarm halving (150% to 75%), and it is only collectable by a Spiritborn build that puts a storm-tagged skill on the bar. If at least one usable Spiritborn skill carries that tag, a build weighted toward it collects roughly 80% increased damage that no poison variant can reach, which would more than cover the halving. If no usable skill carries the tag, the board is unreachable for this class's current bars and the halving is simply a nerf with a decoration attached.
Confidencelow
How to test it[ptr] (1) The only test that matters, and it is the first thing to do on the PTR: open the skill tree and read the tags. Which Spiritborn skills, if any, are Storm skills? No source this repo consulted answers that - the official 3.2.0 notes name the board and its effect and stop, and knowledge/classes/spiritborn.md tags none of the thirteen Season 14 skills. If the answer is 'none that a real bar can use', stop here and record it: that is a genuinely useful finding and it retires this page. (2) If some skill does carry the tag, attach Swarm of Storms and measure the actual multiplier - 'roughly 80%' comes from an aggregator summary, not from the official notes' own wording, so the number itself is soft. (3) Compare against spiritborn-hybrid-counterswarm-direct on the same character: that build assumes the compensation is unavailable, so the two pages are a controlled pair. (4) Check whether the board's bonus stacks with the poison swarm at all, or whether committing to it means giving up the archetype. (5) Note that the board cannot be drawn on this site: it is new in 3.2.0 and the pinned 3.1.0 game database has no grid for it, which is why the paragon layout below records only boards that exist in the feed and names Swarm of Storms in prose instead.
